diagnostic_evidence.quote: This momentum scheme enhances the approximation of the solution by adding the current fixed-point update to the difference between the current and previous updates.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims a rigorous proof that KM momentum accelerates convergence. The formal content proves only that a single extrapolated step $T^{\theta}x$ with $\theta\in(0,2\theta^*)$ (or $[2\theta^*,0]$) is no farther from $\hat x$ than the Picard step $Tx$, and strictly closer only when $\alpha<1/2$. No convergence or rate comparison between a momentum iteration and Picard/KM is proved, and the momentum iteration $x^{k+1}=T^{\theta_k}x^k$ is never shown to converge (TKMA needs the extra $T^2$ damping $t<1$). In addition, $T^{\theta}$ with $\theta>0$ rewrites as $(1-\lambda)x^k+\lambda Tx^k$ with $\lambda=1+\theta>1$, while \eqref{TradKM} stipulates $\lambda_k\in(0,1]$, i.e. $\theta_k\in(-1,0]$; so the scheme claimed to accelerate is not the KM iteration as defined.

failure_location.quote: We rigorously prove that KM momentum accelerates convergence for averaged nonexpansive operators with appropriate momentum parameters.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the result as a strict one-step decrease of $\|T^{\theta}x-\hat x\|$ versus $\|Tx-\hat x\|$ for $\theta\in(0,2\theta^*)$ (strict only for $\alpha<1/2$), describe $T^{\theta}$ as an extrapolated KM step with $\lambda=1+\theta$ rather than as \eqref{TradKM}, and withdraw the convergence-acceleration promise.
issues.overall_effect: Contribution (ii) and the Section 3 claims of "accelerated convergence compared to the original fixed-point iteration" overstate a one-step distance comparison; no convergence-acceleration guarantee survives for the momentum KM iteration itself.
issues.title: Claim that KM momentum "accelerates convergence" exceeds the proved one-step comparison, and the analyzed extrapolation is outside the KM parameter range
issues.why_classification: The repair is a limited weakening of the advertised contribution that leaves a recognizably comparable result (proved one-step improvement) and needs no new argument; but it necessarily withdraws a substantive promised guarantee (accelerated convergence), so it is more than a local routine fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the case $\alpha\in\big[\frac{1}{2},1\big)$, analogous to the proof of Theorem \ref{thm_KMaccel}, we can establish the following result.

issues.failure_explanation: No proof is given. The proof of Theorem thm_KMaccel obtains the sign of $\theta^*$ from $-\langle Tx-x,Tx-\hat x\rangle\ge(1/(2\alpha)-1)\|Tx-x\|^2$, which is vacuous for $\alpha\ge 1/2$. The new assertion that the ball condition $Tx\in O(\hat x_{1/2},\|x-\hat x_{1/2}\|)$ is equivalent to $\theta^*\ge 0$ (and its negation to $\theta^*<0$ strictly) needs the separate identity $\theta^*=(\|x-\hat x_{1/2}\|^2-\|Tx-\hat x_{1/2}\|^2)/\|Tx-x\|^2$, which is established nowhere; hence the stated dichotomy is unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: If $T\bmx\in O(\hx_{1/2},\|\bmx-\hx_{1/2}\|)$, then $\theta^*\geq0$ and $\|T^{\theta}\bmx-\hx\|\leq\|T\bmx-\hx\|$ for $\theta\in[0,2\theta^*]$. Otherwise, $\theta^*<0$ and $\|T^{\theta}\bmx-\hx\|\leq\|T\bmx-\hx\|$ for $\theta\in[2\theta^*,0]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the short computation $\theta^*=(\|x-\hat x_{1/2}\|^2-\|Tx-\hat x_{1/2}\|^2)/\|Tx-x\|^2$ to get the equivalence between the ball condition and $\theta^*\ge0$, then repeat the Pythagorean step of Theorem thm_KMaccel; interpret $O(\cdot,\cdot)$ as a closed ball so that the "otherwise" case yields $\theta^*<0$ strictly.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed extension of the KM-acceleration geometry to $\alpha\in[1/2,1)$ is unproved, so the geometric motivation for the adaptive momentum in this range rests on an unsupported statement.
issues.title: Theorem thm_KMaccel1 is asserted by "analogy" although its key sign dichotomy has no analogue in the cited proof
issues.why_classification: A two-line identity plus the already supplied Pythagorean argument proves the statement; no claim, regime or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that $\alpha\in(0,1/2]$, $T$ is an $\alpha$-averaged nonexpansive operator and $T^{\theta}$ is defined by \eqref{def:Ttheta}.
Let $T$ be an $\alpha$-averaged nonexpansive operator, where $\alpha\in(0,1/2]$, and let $\{\bmx^k\}$ be a sequence generated by \eqref{eq:IKMAiter}.
$\mI-\prox_{\frac{1}{\lambda}\phi}$ is firmly nonexpansive, which is $1/2$-averaged nonexpansive from Remark 4.34 of \cite{bauschke2017convex}
It is easy to see that this operator is averaged nonexpansive when $\alpha\in(0,2/L)$, where $L$ is the Lipschitz constant of $\nabla f$.
The step size parameter $\alpha$ is set to $1.99$.

issues.failure_explanation: All convergence/rate results (Proposition prop:thetarange, Lemmas lem:monotonic, Tthetamoto, Theorems thm:conv, convergerate) assume $T$ is $\alpha$-averaged with $\alpha\in(0,1/2]$, i.e. $T$ is firmly nonexpansive; Proposition prop:thetarange(ii) needs $\alpha(1+\theta_k)\le 1$ so that $T^{\theta_k}$ is nonexpansive. The applications verify only that $T_2=(\mI-\prox_{\phi/\lambda})\circ\mA$ and $T_3=P_{\mathcal C}(I-\alpha\nabla f)$ are "averaged nonexpansive", which allows constants up to 1. These are compositions of a firmly nonexpansive map with a merely nonexpansive one, and such compositions are in general only $\gamma$-averaged with $\gamma>1/2$ (a projection composed with a firmly nonexpansive linear map is $1/2$-averaged only in degenerate cases). For the stated parameters the constants are about $0.999$ ($\lambda=0.999/4$ makes $\mI-\lambda\bmB\bmB^\top$ have eigenvalue near $-1$) and $0.995$ (step $1.99>1/L=1$). Hence the theorems are invoked outside their hypotheses. The hypothesis cannot simply be dropped: for averaging constants above $1/2$ the momentum step $T^{\theta_k}$ can be expansive and TKMA can diverge.

failure_location.quote: Thus operator $T_2$ defined by \eqref{operatorTfordenoising} is averaged nonexpansive when $\lambda<\frac{1}{4}$. According to \eqref{eq:IKMAiter}, the complete iterative scheme of the TKMA for solving model \eqref{TVdenoise} is given as follows.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In both applications replace $T$ by $S=(1-\beta)\mI+\beta T$ with $\beta=1/(2\gamma)$ for an averaging constant $\gamma$ of $T$; $S$ is $1/2$-averaged with $Fix(S)=Fix(T)$, so Theorems thm:conv and convergerate apply verbatim to TKMA on $S$ and every conclusion and rate survives, at the cost of changing the iteration and recomputing the experiments. Alternatively restrict the scope to firmly nonexpansive $T$ and withdraw the guarantees for \eqref{TVdenoise} and \eqref{lowmatrix}.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence and $o(1/\sqrt{k})$ guarantees do not cover TKMA as specified in the two algorithm boxes; the claims that these procedures output the denoised image $\bmu=\bmx-\lambda\bmB^\top\bmy^K$ and the completed matrix $\bmX^K$ are unproved.
issues.title: Convergence theory assumes T is at most 1/2-averaged, but the TV-denoising and matrix-completion operators are only established (and only able) to be averaged with larger constants
issues.why_classification: A contained construction (relaxing the operator while keeping its fixed points) plus a rerun of the experiments restores every advertised claim and rate without new global proof architecture, but the algorithmic iteration and the numerical study must change, so the loss exceeds a local routine edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Finally, we present in Figure \ref{sumthetak} the plots $\sum_{k=0}^{n} |\theta_{k+1}-\theta_k|$ for TKMA against its iteration count $n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The figure displays only finitely many partial sums $\sum_{k=0}^n|\theta_{k+1}-\theta_k|$. Apparent stabilization over a bounded range of $n$ cannot establish convergence of the infinite series, so the hypothesis of Theorem \ref{convergerate} is not verified and the asserted "ensuring" of the $o(1/\sqrt{k})$ rate does not follow.

failure_location.quote: This experimentally verifies that the condition $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} |\theta_{k+1}-\theta_k|<+\infty$ in Theorem \ref{convergerate} is satisfied in the denoising scenario, thereby ensuring the convergence rate of TKMA as established by the theorem.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claim by the supported statement that the plotted partial sums stay bounded over the tested range, which is consistent with (but does not verify) the hypothesis of Theorem \ref{convergerate}.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the rate hypothesis of Theorem \ref{convergerate} holds in the denoising experiment, and hence that the rate guarantee applies to the reported runs, is unsupported.
issues.title: Finite plot claimed to "experimentally verify" convergence of an infinite series and thereby ensure the rate hypothesis
issues.why_classification: A short local rewording preserves the theorem, the figure and all mathematical guarantees; only the false assertion of verification is dropped.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the maximum rank $r > 0$; the step size $\alpha > 0$
In this experiment, we consider a $100\times 100$ matrix and explore both the scenarios of rank $r=30$ and $r=50$.
In our experiments, the ground-truth matrix $\bmA$ was generated as a low-rank product $\bmU\bmV^{\top}$, where $\bmU$ and $\bmV$ are n-by-r matrices with entries sampled from a normal distribution.

issues.failure_explanation: The constraint $\|X\|_*\le r$ bounds the sum of singular values, not the rank: $\mathrm{diag}(r/(2n),\ldots,r/(2n))$ satisfies it with full rank $n>r$, while a rank-one matrix $\sigma uu^\top$ is excluded whenever $\sigma>r$. So the feasible set is not "rank at most $r$", and the algorithm inputs ("the maximum rank $r>0$") feed a nuclear-norm radius into $P_{\mathcal C}$. With $r$ set equal to the rank of the ground truth and $\bmA=\bmU\bmV^\top$ built from normal entries, $\|\bmA\|_*$ is far larger than $r$, so $\bmA$ is not feasible and \eqref{lowmatrix} cannot return it; the experiment is not a matrix-completion test of the stated kind.

failure_location.quote: where $P_{\Omega}$ denotes the projection onto a randomly sampled index set $\Omega$, $r$ is the supposed maximum rank, and the nuclear norm constraint $\|\bmX\|_{\ast}\leq r$ is applied to enforce a low-rank solution.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Separate the two parameters: constrain $\mathrm{rank}(X)\le r$ (or state explicitly that a nuclear-norm ball of radius $\tau$ is the convex relaxation) and choose $\tau$ at the scale of $\|\bmA\|_*$ (or normalize the data), then rerun the matrix completion experiments with the corrected feasible set.
issues.overall_effect: The model \eqref{lowmatrix}, both algorithm boxes' input contracts and the interpretation of the low-rank matrix completion experiments are internally inconsistent; the claimed demonstration of TKMA "for low-rank matrix completion" does not establish completion of a rank-$r$ matrix.
issues.title: Nuclear-norm radius r conflated with a maximum rank in the low-rank matrix completion model
issues.why_classification: The defect is a modelling/parameter inconsistency that must be repaired by redefining the constraint radius and re-optimizing the experiments, but it needs no new proof architecture and leaves the convergence theory and the rest of the paper recognizably intact.
